claims.text: the hit set holds every reference to TOP_LEVEL, CHILD_KEYS, export_shell over the name forms this pass searched
validate() refuses `topology` and `team-patterns` as unknown top-level keys until both are added to TOP_LEVEL; with TOP_LEVEL grown the sample validates clean.
Growing TOP_LEVEL alone validates nothing below the new keys: a misspelled role field, a list as a stage value and a stage naming a pattern that does not exist all pass validate().

CHILD_KEYS validates a map one level down against a fixed key set; a map keyed by free stage names or free pattern names cannot be listed there, and the loop at afk-config.py:586 skips any top-level key not listed, so both new keys need their own validation code, as `investigation` has (afk-config.py:637-667).

The parity test iterates CHILD_KEYS only: a CONFIG.md map row with no CHILD_KEYS entry passes (the `investigation` row is the precedent), and adding either new key to CHILD_KEYS fails the test unless its CONFIG.md row backticks exactly the listed child keys and no other key-shaped word.

The YAML subset parser reads a stage-to-pattern map, a pattern-to-record map, a list of role maps written `- name: x` with sibling keys, and a scalar list nested in a role; it refuses flow lists and maps, a list of lists, and a non-ASCII key.

export-shell flattens the new blocks to AFK_CFG_TOPOLOGY_<STAGE> and AFK_CFG_TEAM_PATTERNS_<PATTERN>_ROLES_<i>_<FIELD> plus _COUNT lines; every name is a valid shell identifier, but shell_name maps free keys many-to-one (`to-prd`, `to_prd` and `To-Prd` share one name; a `roles-count` key overwrites the `roles` list count), and the last line wins on eval with no error.

export-shell runs load() without validate(), so the new keys export before TOP_LEVEL grows; a parse error in a new block makes export-shell exit 2, and hooks/lib/config.sh:29 swallows it, leaving every AFK_CFG_* name unset for every gate in that shell.
afk_config_list reads only lists of scalars: for a list of role maps it prints empty lines, so a bash consumer of roles must use afk_config_get (JSON) or the Python reader.

deep_merge merges maps key by key and replaces lists whole: a local overlay that changes one role's model replaces the full roles list of that pattern, while an overlay changing one topology stage keeps the others.

get() answers topology.<stage> and team-patterns.<pattern>.roles.<i>.model; a stage name holding a dot is accepted by the parser but unreachable by get (exit 1), and get does not answer the `.count` names export-shell writes.
normalize() folds only the investigation block's paths and leaves the new blocks unchanged.

Readers that call validate() break if a configuration carries the new keys before TOP_LEVEL grows: seed_map.load_config raises ConfigError (investigation seed exits 2), publish.sh sets cfg_ok=0 so an agent run queues with reason config-invalid, and test_self_config_validates goes red if the plugin's own .afk/config.yaml adds them first. TOP_LEVEL must ship with or before any configuration using the keys.

Load-only readers (tracker MCP server, tracker_api, github-issues api, run-hook, setup_secrets, create-worktree, collect_env) read one fixed key and are unchanged by well-formed new blocks; on a parse error server.py fails at start-up, tracker_api raises, and run-hook.py falls back to the default manifest.

No existing shell-view reader can collide with the new names: every reader reads a fixed name under an existing top-level prefix, no existing prefix is a prefix of AFK_CFG_TOPOLOGY or AFK_CFG_TEAM_PATTERNS, and worktree-provision's compgen loop only re-exports the extra names.

Tests to add: the TYPOS table and typo test cover no new block, test_unknown_top_level_key_is_refused stays green, and no test pins shell-name collisions, dangling pattern references, or the new blocks in the agreement fixture.
CONFIG.md's YAML subset already expresses a stage-to-pattern map, a pattern-name-to-record map and a list of role maps; no parser or subset edit is needed
CONFIG.md's schema table needs two new map rows, and the parity test cannot fail on them because it iterates CHILD_KEYS only; free-keyed maps cannot enter CHILD_KEYS
CONFIG.md:113-116 and CONFIG.md:228-230 state every map is validated and pinned one level down; both become false for the two free-keyed maps and must carve them out

The shell view exports nested maps and lists of maps by full path and folds '-', '.', '_' and case to one name, so two distinct stage keys can overwrite one AFK_CFG_ variable; CONFIG.md:234-244 documents neither
A stage key containing a dot parses but is unreachable through afk-config.py get, so CONFIG.md should constrain stage names
A local overlay overriding one team pattern replaces that pattern's roles list whole while other patterns survive
